text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like this, TSLA and its analogs delivered a median 20-session return of 2.96%, with 68% of outcomes finishing above zero. The single number to anchor on is the 10th percentile of that distribution: -8.68%. That is what the bad tail looked like historically when the state matched this one.

[state]
The engine pulled these 50 analogs from 39 distinct sessions across 30 symbols because the current feature vector is defined by three unusual tensions. First, short-term volatility has collapsed relative to the recent past: the 5d/20d volatility ratio sits at 0.489 (z-score -1.217). Second, dollar volume is thin, with the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score at -1.558 (z-score used -1.026). Third, WTI crude oil surged 19.24% over 20 days (z-score 1.124), an outlier macro input. These combine with a stock sitting -26.98% off its 52-week high, a 20-session realised volatility of 48.97%, and a drawdown of -14.35% from its 60-session peak. The retrieval spans from 2016-12-14 to 2026-08-17, heavily weighted toward 2025 (20 analogs) and 2026 (12 analogs), pulling in Technology (12), ETF China (8), and China ADR (7) names alongside Consumer Disc. peers. Only 1 of the 50 analogs is TSLA itself.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs, the mean 20-session forward return was 2.39% and the median was 2.96%, with a standard deviation of 6.9%. The distribution carries a slight negative skew of -0.288. The interquartile range ran from -1.25% at the 25th percentile to 6.87% at the 75th percentile, while the 90th percentile reached 10.51%. In 18% of the episodes, the return fell below -5%, and in 4% it fell below -10%. No episode breached -20%.

The worst outcome in the set was Li Auto (LI) on 2025-09-22, which returned -11.47%. The next worst was Boeing (BA) on 2021-08-04 at -3.76%. The best outcome was 15.49%. The closest match by distance was Thermo Fisher (TMO) on 2025-08-07 (distance 0.4262), which returned 8.33%. Schlumberger (SLB) on 2026-08-04 (distance 0.4336) returned 12.48%. The only TSLA analog, dated 2025-08-07 (distance 0.4374), returned 8.87%.

[tails]
A position can finish near the median and still be un-holdable through the path. Across the 50 analogs, the median maximum adverse excursion was -3.53%. At the 10th percentile, the max adverse excursion reached -10.99%, and at the 25th percentile it was -7.38%. On the upside, the median maximum favourable excursion was 6.73%, reaching 9.45% at the 75th percentile and 14.07% at the 90th percentile. This yields a historical reward-to-risk ratio of 1.91.

Looking at specific drawdown thresholds during the 20-session horizon: there was a 40% probability of breaching a 5% drawdown, a 14% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown, and a 0% probability of breaching either a 15% or 20% drawdown.

[stress]
The stress scenarios that materially worsen the baseline median of 2.96% are led by rate and liquidity regimes. Under the 2022 inflation / rate bear scenario, the median forward return drops to -7.83% (a delta of -10.79%), with a 74% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash produces a median of -3.2% (delta -6.16%) and a 10th percentile of -30.58%; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare yields a median of -6.29% (delta -9.25%) with a 50% probability of a 10% drawdown; caveat: ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs.

Among shock scenarios, the earnings release day stress shifts the median to -1.18% (delta -4.14%) with a 20% probability of falling below -10%; caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The crypto drawdown contagion scenario pushes the median to -1.99% (delta -4.95%); caveat: the BTC feature is a market-wide regime proxy, and any name-level linkage to crypto flows is not identified here. The volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX) results in a median of -2.28% (delta -5.24%); caveat: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value. The 2025-04 tariff shock gives a median of -0.86% (delta -3.82%) but a 61.5% probability of a 10% drawdown; caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind shows a median of -0.03% (delta -2.99%) but a 44.4% probability of a 10% drawdown; caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though intra-horizon excursion did not. The liquidity air pocket yields a median of 0.13% (delta -2.83%); caveat: gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not a 7x24 venue, and for the verified wrapper TSLAG_USDT, 46.68% of realised hourly movement happened while the reference market was closed. The policy-rate path re-pricing (+1.5 sigma) gives a median of -0.66% (delta -3.62%); caveat: uses DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels as proxies, and transmission depends on duration and balance sheet not featured here.

Scenarios that do not materially worsen the baseline include the 2023-03 regional bank stress (median 3.07%, delta 0.11%; caveat: very short window dominated by a handful of sessions), the FOMC decision day (median 1.7%, delta -1.26%; caveat: only 92 decision days exist, making the analog set small and highly overlapping), and the China ADR de-rating (median 1%, delta -1.96%; caveat: delisting and audit-access risks are structural and will not appear in a price/vol feature space). No scenarios were skipped.

[limits]
This analysis describes a historical conditional distribution, not a forecast. The engine's own validation states explicitly: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The conformal interval achieves 87.4% out-of-sample coverage against an 80% target, but its matched coverage width is 23.42% versus 22.66% for the unconditional name benchmark, confirming it does not beat the naive approach on sharpness. The directional hit rate is 54%. The PIT chi-square statistic is 363.9, far above the 5% critical value of 16.92.

Provenance relies on 2513 sessions across 71 symbols using 25 metric features. Prices are sourced keyless from api.stockanalysis.com. Earnings dates use SEC full-text search clustered at 6 calendar days. Only 1 of the 50 analogs is TSLA itself.

If traded via the tokenised wrapper TSLAG_USDT on Gate.io spot v4, the status is "measured" and it is a "fair tracker". The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 46.68% of the wrapper's own realised hourly price movement landed in those shut hours. Daily returns correlate at 0.9561 with a tracking error of 100 bp/day. The premium band over the underlying's last raw close of 364.27 runs from -0.43% to 0.41% (p10 to p90), with the wrapper last trading at 380.08. The spread is 5 bps. As the card notes, a fair tracker is not the underlying, and at 100 bp/day of tracking error the wrapper carries its own idiosyncratic risk outside cash hours.
